name: False Flag — Real Attack with Contradictory Attribution
description: A real compromise: process hollowing and credential dumping confirmed in memory (hard-to-fake structural evidence). On top of the real attack, the operator planted Cyrillic strings whose profile contradicts the actual TTPs and OPSEC — the cultural markers are too pristine and inconsistent with the actor's toolchain. CAIE fracture: FALSE_FLAG_ATTRIBUTION_MISMATCH. The malice belongs to the planter, not to any Russian-speaker.
audit_note: Reconstructed post H-02 fix. Previous version (cultural-high + technical-low) was forensically equivalent to a clean foreign machine — indistinguishable without explicit manipulation evidence. This version has: (1) confirmed malicious event, (2) attribution markers contradicting the TTP profile. That is what a false flag looks like.

artifacts.description: Process hollowing in svchost.exe confirmed in memory (T1055.012). Reflective DLL injection detected. Hard-to-fake structural evidence of a real intrusion.
LSASS credential dumping detected (T1003.001). Active compromise confirmed.

Cyrillic strings injected into the dropper: suspiciously pristine, inconsistent with the actor's actual toolchain and OPSEC. Attribution markers contradict the observed technical TTP profile. Placement is too clean for a native speaker.
